- A) 0.1 A
- B) 0.5 A
- C) 1.0 A
- D) 1.2 A "C. (1.0 V / 1200 Ω) × 1200 = 1.0 A. The common module ships with 1.2 kΩ → 1 A. For a small cell you raise R_PROG (e.g.
column2: 2 kΩ → ≈ 0.6 A)."	"week-01 mcq"

- C) Adds a component to the BOM

Sat 17 Oct · Topic of Fri 16 Oct: schematic conventions, the TP4056 + DW01A + FS8205A charger · Q3 · MCQ

In the protection circuit, the FS8205A is:
- A) A single N-MOSFET
- B) A dual N-MOSFET in one package, used back-to-back in the battery negative path
- C) A dual P-MOSFET in the positive path
- D) A resettable fuse "B. Two N-MOSFETs with sources tied together
column2: driven by the DW01A's OD (discharge) and OC (charge) outputs. Their body diodes point in opposite directions
column3: so the IC can block discharge and charge independently."	"week-01 mcq"

Status LED on 5 V, red LED with V_F ≈ 2.0 V, target 2 mA. Resistor value and power? Which E24 value do you pick? "R = (5 − 2.0) / 0.002 = 1.5 kΩ (E24 value exists). Sat 17 Oct · Topic of Fri 16 Oct: schematic conventions, the TP4056 + DW01A + FS8205A charger · Q6 · Calc

TP4056 at 5.0 V input charging a cell at 3.7 V with 1 A. Power dissipated in the IC? What does the IC do about it, and what are your two design options? "P = (5.0 − 3.7) × 1 = 1.3 W in a SOP-8 with a thermal pad. The TP4056 has thermal regulation: it reduces the charge current when the die reaches about 120 °C
column2: so charging just gets slower. Options: 1. lower the current (R_PROG = 2 kΩ → ≈ 0.6 A → ≈ 0.8 W); 2. more copper under the thermal pad with vias to the bottom layer. This is exactly why linear chargers stop making sense above ≈ 1 A."	"week-01 calc"

The 10 µF input capacitor of the TP4056 must end up next to the VCC pin on the PCB. How do you make that intent survive from schematic to layout? "Draw it beside the IC pin on the schematic (not in a ""caps"" corner)

column3: and in the PCB place the IC first and the cap second
column4: before anything else in that block. Placement Transfer from the schematic helps keep blocks together."	"week-01 apply"

Sat 17 Oct · Topic of Fri 16 Oct: schematic conventions, the TP4056 + DW01A + FS8205A charger · Q8 · Interview

"What does a Li-ion protection IC protect against, and why are there two MOSFETs?" Answer aloud in 60 s. "Model answer: ""It watches the cell voltage and the current through the MOSFETs. It opens the charge switch on over-voltage
column2: about 4.3 V on the DW01A
column3: opens the discharge switch on under-voltage
column5: and on over-current or short circuit it trips fast using the voltage drop across the MOSFETs. Two MOSFETs are needed because a single MOSFET's body diode always conducts in one direction; two back-to-back let the IC block charging and discharging separately. Check the exact thresholds in the datasheet."""	"week-01 interview"

Using the IPC-2221 outer-layer rule for 1 oz copper and a 10 °C rise, roughly what trace width carries 1 A? What width do you use for the TP4056 1 A charge path, and why wider? "About 0.3 mm (≈ 12 mil) for 1 A at 10 °C rise on an outer layer

"Describe your placement strategy for a small 2-layer board." Answer aloud in 60 s. "Model answer: ""Connectors go on the edges where the mechanics need them. Then I place by functional block
column2: following the schematic: the regulator and its caps together
column3: the MCU with its decoupling caps touching the pins

Mon 19 Oct · Topic of Sun 18 Oct: the review checklist, first library device from a datasheet · Q1 · MCQ

Footprint pad sizes should come from:
- A) A guess from the part photo
- B) The datasheet's recommended land pattern (or the IPC-7351 pattern for that package)
- C) Another part that looks similar
- D) The smallest size that passes DRC "B. The land pattern is designed for solder-joint reliability and reflow behaviour. ""Looks similar"" is how a 0.5 mm pitch part lands on a 0.65 mm footprint." "week-01 mcq"

A clear pin-1 mark on the footprint silkscreen matters because:
- A) The 3D model needs it
- B) Assembly and inspection use it for orientation; a polarized part placed backwards is a dead board
- C) DRC requires it
- D) The autorouter uses it "B. Pin 1 dot
column2: cathode bar
column3: ""+"" on electrolytics. Also check the pick-and-place rotation against the 3D view; the mark is what the assembler's operator compares against."	"week-01 mcq"

Mon 19 Oct · Topic of Sun 18 Oct: the review checklist, first library device from a datasheet · Q3 · MCQ

In EasyEDA Pro, the library object that binds a symbol, a footprint and a 3D model is the:
- A) Reuse block
- B) Device
- C) Net class
- D) Panel library "B. Device. A reuse block is a copied circuit fragment; a net class is a rule group; the panel library is for panel shapes." "week-01 mcq"

Mon 19 Oct · Topic of Sun 18 Oct: the review checklist, first library device from a datasheet · Q4 · MCQ

The courtyard of a footprint is:
- A) The copper pad area
- B) The keep-out area around body + pads that other parts must not enter
- C) The silkscreen outline
- D) The solder-paste opening "B. It is what placement DRC uses to stop parts from colliding and to leave room for the pick-and-place nozzle and rework." "week-01 mcq"

Mon 19 Oct · Topic of Sun 18 Oct: the review checklist, first library device from a datasheet · Q5 · Calc

A connector has 0.5 mm pitch and 0.3 mm-wide pads. What is the gap between adjacent pads? Can a 0.127 mm trace with 0.127 mm clearance pass between two pads? "Gap = 0.5 − 0.3 = 0.2 mm. A trace between them needs 0.127 + 2 × 0.127 = 0.381 mm > 0.2 mm → no. Route out from the pad ends
column2: and use the inner layers or the other side for crossings. This is why fine-pitch connectors push boards to 4 layers."	"week-01 calc"
